title:
MZ VisuStella Message Core: Using both line break (
) and wait for button input (/!) during auto wrap?

posts.author: LaCipolla
posts.body:
Hi everybody, I'm using the auto wrap feature of VisuStella Message Core and the ODW Multi-Language System . I also make extensive use of line breaks (
) and wait for button input (/!), sometimes together, to structure and pace dialogues. Usually it works and I like it that way! But sometimes, when these two tags interact with auto wrap, there can be a problem because auto wrap does its automatic line break (at the end of a line) or automatic button input (at the end of a message window), and I end up with a free line, a double button input, an empty space at the beginning of the line or some weirder stuff. Most of that is obvious to me, but in some cases the interactions behave REALLY weirdly. Essentially, I have to "micromanage" a lot, with A LOT of trial and error. And more often than I would like, these interactions even force me to seriously change the content of the text in favour of a visually alright text window. Now, I thought about bringing specific examples ... But honestly, it would be a pain because it's a big collection of very specific situations, and in general, I'm more interested in how other people approach this tension. How do you deal with this? Do you have experiences or tips? Thanks!

This seems like it's necessary. While I don't use these specific plugins, I do use Yanfly's Message Core with word wrapping, and I've never encountered the issue.
The method that parses escape codes and determines where to break lines should not be registering \! as characters that take up space on the line. So, if anything, if you can reproduce this issue it seems like it ought to be a bug report to VisuStella.

posts.author: r66r
posts.body:
This is just a guess (it's impossible to know how VS designed the autowrap function), but it's based on what I've seen in other plugins with autowrap.
To create the line break, the plugin creates the line of text word by word and checks at each iteration whether or not the length in pixels of the line exceeds the width of the window. If it does, the line break is added before the last word added... and so on for each line. That's why, in your example, the line break occurs after the word "There" => the width of the line is always less than the width of the window at that point.
